key_insight: Machine-learned molecular dynamics predicts that approximately 0.5% biaxial tensile strain drives MAPbI₃ from tetragonal to cubic at 300 K while increasing its ensemble-averaged band gap.
engineering_relevance: Finite-temperature strain modeling can guide epitaxial engineering of perovskite absorber phases and optical properties where static calculations miss dynamic disorder.
method: Train machine-learned force fields on-the-fly using DFT.
Run nanosecond-long bulk and free-standing slab simulations with fixed in-plane lattice vectors at 300 K.
Track lattice symmetry, octahedral tilts, molecular orientations, and band gaps averaged over MD snapshots.
evidence_signal: The predicted transition and tensile-strain band-gap blue shift agree with reported experiments, while bulk and slab models show consistent trends.
watch_item: Static averaged structures predict the opposite band-gap trend, making finite-temperature sampling essential for reliable strain-response predictions.
paper_title: Strain-Induced Tetragonal-to-Cubic Transition in MAPbI$_3$ from Machine-Learned Molecular Dynamics
